name: Psychedelic Art
visualIdentity: Flowing curves, saturated waves, vortices and looping geometry form an organized, continuous visual theme. Color and shapes may morph; distorted lettering is decorative, while key information needs stable, readable moments.
suitableUses: Explicitly suited to psychedelic and demoscene imagery, infinite zooms, kaleidoscopic transitions and surreal or abstract spatial passages. Music visuals and festival titles are suggested uses. For interactive HTML, shader fields and optional progress-driven storytelling can suit the style; this is an inferred fit.
limitations: Dense text is difficult to read during travel; preserve reading holds. Avoid hidden resets in one-shot sequences, disorienting motion where stable orientation is needed, and unrelated stacked effects. Reduce or omit motion when the subject calls for it. Motion-pattern candidates are optional and should be used only when their action fits the scene.
palette: Use task-provided exact colors, approved references and existing semantic mappings first. Otherwise, the suggested five-token palette is background #201337, foreground #FFF3DB, accents #D957A5, #DA873F and #7464D2. These are suggestions, not canonical colors. Gradients are optional for organized wave fields, using the three accents as Lab stops; samples do not add base colors. Preserve approved values and roles. The suggested #7464D2 with #FFF3DB misses the normal-text contrast target; place body text on a suitable existing backing and verify actual composites.
motionAndInteraction: Use continuous shader-driven color fields and repeated geometry with a shared time value; composite readable text separately. Video motion must be deterministic and seekable, with one owner per animated property. Interactive HTML may map finite scroll progress to a vortex passage, chapter handoff, or story stages when semantically appropriate; support coherent reverse states, keyboard/touch use and reduced motion. Holds, bounded morphs and loop continuity matter.
audio: No fixed soundtrack is specified. Choose music, voice, vocals, effects, ambience or silence for the topic and explicit audio requirements. Music may structure morphs, but avoid beat-strobing and preserve speech and reading space. Use authorized assets; verify synchronization, intelligibility, balance and clipping.
assetRequirements: No specific source assets are required. Prepare and load fonts and media locally; preserve supplied artwork, exact colors and copy. Procedural or cached geometry should be deterministic. Distorted lettering may ornament, but keep essential text separately readable. Audio assets must be authorized; unspecified inputs should not be assumed available.
combinations: Suggested: style-105 musical section timing can structure shader morphs, with stable title holds; style-007 Art Nouveau curves can frame the field if ornament follows its flow and avoids obscuring text. Keep the violet, pink and amber system. Avoid unrelated effects, beat-strobing, Nouveau greens and over-distorted information text.
productionApproach: Select the style renderer and motion method for the visual goal: WebGL/GLSL can render full-screen fields, with Three.js where geometry needs it; these are recommendations, not a mandatory bundle. Keep composition/export separate. HyperFrames is primary; Remotion is allowed only if unavailable or a verified required capability is missing, with the reason recorded. Drive video from seekable composition time, then inspect key frames and the full render. For HTML, adapt interaction to finite, reversible progress and a usable reduced-motion state. Audio choice and production details are task-dependent; unspecified.
